statement.p: Consider the graphs of f(x) and g(x) below:

image.shortdescription: Graph of two functions and some points on the functions.

description.p: Function f starts at the origin, goes up and back down to the x-axis and then up higher and then back down to the axis again, with the two peaks at x=2.2 and x=6.1. It hits the x-axis at x=0, x=4, and x=8. Function g is an increasing line going though the points occuring at the two peaks of f, that is, (2.2, f(2.2)) and (6.1,f(6.1)).

statement.p: For each interval given below, decide whether the average rate of change of f(x) is positive, negative, or zero over that particular interval.

row.cell: Sign of Average Rate of Change of f(x)

solution.p: The average rate of change of a function can be approximated graphically by looking at the steepness of the line segment connecting the two endpoints of the interval on the graph of f(x). If the line segment is going up, the average rate of change over the interval is positive. If the line segment is going down, the average rate of change over the interval is negative. If the line segment is horizontal, the average rate of change over the interval is zero. Based on this interpretation, you should determine the following answers:
